Although all AEs are recorded in the CRF after signing informed consent, SAE reporting to the sponsor begins after the patient has signed informed consent and has received investigational product. However, if an SAE occurs after signing informed consent, but prior to receiving investigational product, AND is considered reasonably possibly related to a study procedure then it MUST be reported.

Pregnancy (maternal or paternal exposure to investigational product) does not meet the definition of an AE. However, to fulfill regulatory requirements any pregnancy should be reported following the SAE process to collect data on the outcome for both mother and fetus.

Nonserious AEs obtained through the questionnaire are recorded and analyzed separately. Only SAEs elicited through the Nasal and Non_nasal Score Questionnaire and Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale are to be recorded as AEs via CRF and reported to Lilly or its designee within 24 hours as SAEs.

data.text: Refer to the LY900018 IB and GlucaGen Summary of Product Characteristics for more information regarding overdose.

Unscheduled orthostatic vital signs should be assessed, if possible, during any AE of dizziness or posture_induced symptoms. If orthostatic measurements are required, patients should be supine for at least 5 minutes and stand for at least 2 minutes. If the patient feels unable to stand, supine vital signs only will be recorded.
Single ECGs will be collected and stored locally at the investigator's site. Triplicate ECGs will be electronically transmitted to a central ECG laboratory designated by Lilly.

If a hypoglycemic event meets the criteria of severe, it needs to be recorded as serious in the CRF (that is, recorded as an SAE). In the case of a hypoglycemic event (other than severe), the actual glucose value, if measured, should be recorded in the CRF, with any treatments administered, and not be recorded as an AE.
Cases of hypoglycemia may be treated with foods rich in carbohydrate such as fruit, juice, skimmed milk, or energy bars.

The bedside PG level, measured using a glucose analyzer (Antsense Duo, HORIBA Ltd. or equivalent), must be 90 to 250 mg/dL to start the procedure. If the bedside PG is outside of this range, the hypoglycemia induction should be rescheduled.

If the target bedside PG level cannot be achieved within 4 hours after the start of insulin infusion, the hypoglycemia induction procedure will be terminated before glucagon administration, and the patient may have a carbohydrate_rich meal and be discharged from the CRU after medical assessment. The patient may be rescheduled for a new dosing visit 1 to 7 days later.

data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non_inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin_induced hypoglycemia using a non_inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) or type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who are eligible for insulin_induced hypoglycemia treatment, enrolled in a 2_period crossover design with at least 66 completers (at least 30 patients with T1DM and 30 patients with T2DM) (Intent_to_Treat (ITT) Population _ all randomized patients completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome) Summary measure: Difference in proportions (percentage of patients achieving treatment success: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2_sided 95% confidence interval based on the 1_sample mean of paired differences; non_inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non_inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study treatment discontinuation before endpoint assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study treatment or withdraws from the study before completing both treatment periods with an evaluable primary outcome within 30 minutes post_glucagon administration

intercurrentEvents.name: Use of additional treatments to increase plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives additional treatments (e.g., intravenous glucose, additional glucagon) to increase plasma glucose within 30 minutes after glucagon administration, which is incorporated into the definition of treatment failure (composite outcome)

intercurrentEvents.name: Failure to achieve adequate insulin_induced hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not achieve the required hypoglycemic nadir (minimum PG at time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration) necessary for a valid treatment period assessment

intercurrentEvents.name: Patient replacement due to non_evaluable primary outcome
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues before completion of both periods with evaluable primary outcome and is replaced; replaced patients are excluded from the primary analysis population

data.text: male patients: agree to use an effective method of contraception for the duration of the study and for 28 days following the last study treatment

data.name: Female contraception and pregnancy requirements
data.text: female patients: [3a] women of childbearing potential who are abstinent (if this is complete abstinence, as their preferred and usual lifestyle) or in a same sex relationship (as part of their preferred and usual lifestyle) must agree to either remain abstinent or stay in a same sex relationship without sexual relationships with males. Periodic abstinence (eg, calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, post_ovulation methods), declaration of abstinence just for the duration of a trial, and withdrawal are not acceptable methods of contraception. [3b] otherwise, women of childbearing potential participating must agree to use one highly effective method (less than 1% failure rate) of contraception, or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception for the entirety of the study. [A] women of childbearing potential participating must test negative for pregnancy prior to initiation of treatment as indicated by a negative serum pregnancy test at the screening visit followed by a negative urine pregnancy test within 24 hours prior to exposure. [B] either one highly effective method of contraception or a combination of 2 effective methods of contraception will be used. The patient may choose to use a double barrier method of contraception. Barrier protection methods without concomitant use of a spermicide are not a reliable or acceptable method. Thus, each barrier method must include use of a spermicide. It should be noted that the use of male and female condoms as a double barrier method is not considered acceptable due to the high failure rate when these methods are combined. [3c] women not of childbearing potential may participate, and include those who are: [A] infertile due to surgical sterilization (hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, or tubal ligation), congenital anomaly such as mullerian agenesis; Or [B] postmenopausal, defined as either: [i] a woman at least 50 years of age with an intact uterus, not on hormone therapy, who has had either: [a] cessation of menses for at least 1 year, or [b] at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea with a follicle_stimulating hormone >40 mIU/mL; or [ii] a woman 55 or older not on hormone therapy, who has had at least 6 months of spontaneous amenorrhea, or [iii] a woman at least 55 years of age with a diagnosis of menopause prior to starting hormone replacement therapy

data.text: A discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator; if both agree it is medically appropriate to continue, documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP is required to allow continuation with or without continued treatment.

data.text: Patients undergo screening within 28 days prior to enrollment (Days _28 to _2) and must meet all enrollment criteria; prior to study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1 patients are randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (LY900018 then IMG, or IMG then LY900018).

data.name: Period 1 to Washout Transition
data.text: After completion of Period 1 Day 1 procedures (including 240_minute assessments, carbohydrate_rich meal, and at least 6 hours post_dose observation), patients are discharged and enter the washout period.

data.name: Washout to Period 2 Transition
data.text: Period 2 dosing occurs after a washout period of 3 to 14 days following Period 1 dosing; admission occurs on Period 2 Day _1 and can be rescheduled if PG is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow_up Transition
data.text: Patients return for a follow_up visit 26 to 30 days (28±2 days) after the last study treatment.

data.name: Follow_up to Additional TE ADA Follow_up Transition
data.text: Patients with treatment_emergent antidrug antibodies at follow_up/ED enter additional follow_up with immunogenicity samples every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until titer returns to baseline or until 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Crossover Treatment Sequence Assignment
data.text: Patients randomized to a treatment sequence receive the alternate treatment in Period 2 (single 3_mg nasal LY900018 or single 1_mg IM glucagon 1 mg).

data.name: Gated Dosing After Interim Safety Review
data.text: Dosing of remaining patients is held until the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist review available safety data from the first 6 patients administered LY900018 in Period 2 (after Period 2 Day 1) and confirm no clinically significant safety findings.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop Rule
data.text: The IV insulin infusion used to induce hypoglycemia is stopped once bedside plasma glucose is <60 mg/dL; study drug is administered approximately 5 minutes later.

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.text: If there is insufficient response to glucagon administration, procedures specified in Section 9.2.4 (Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration) are followed; a carbohydrate_rich meal and prandial insulin dose may be administered as needed to stabilize PG.

data.name: Discontinuation for Concurrent Research Participation
data.text: Patients will be discontinued for enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical, Safety, or Regulatory Reasons
data.text: Patients will be discontinued if participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken and Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: If a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria was inadvertently enrolled, the patient is discontinued unless the Lilly CP/CRP and investigator agree it is medically appropriate to continue and documented approval is obtained.

data.name: Study Termination for Safety
data.text: Following the review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the Investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow_up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities, including the Follow_up/ED visit (within 28±2 days after last study treatment).

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome and the follow_up visit 26 to 30 days after the last study treatment (plus additional TE ADA follow_up if applicable, until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose).

data.name: Lost to Follow_up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow_up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site, after diligent attempts by site personnel.

data.name: Termination of the Study by Sponsor/Investigator
data.description: The study may be stopped following review of safety data from the first 6 patients completing Period 2 Day 1 if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the Investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Exit Due to Inadvertent Enrollment (Ineligibility)
data.description: Patients identified as not meeting enrollment criteria are discontinued unless documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP permits continuation.

data.name: Admission/Dosing Eligibility Decision (Plasma Glucose Check)
data.description: On Day 1 of each period, PG must be 90 to 250 mg/dL and insulin regimen acceptable to proceed with hypoglycemia induction; otherwise admission is rescheduled.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop / Study Drug Administration Decision
data.description: Bedside PG monitoring (≤10 min intervals when PG ≥90 mg/dL, ≤5 min when <90 mg/dL) determines when to stop insulin infusion (PG <60 mg/dL) and administer study drug ~5 minutes later.

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision After First 6 Patients
data.description: Investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist review safety data from the first 6 patients after completion of Period 2 Day 1; dosing of remaining patients proceeds only if no clinically significant safety findings, otherwise the study may be stopped.

data.name: Glucagon Response Assessment / Rescue Decision
data.description: Assessment of response to glucagon administration; insufficient response triggers rescue procedures per Section 9.2.4.

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: After all PK sampling and a carbohydrate_rich meal, with stable PG, patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration or remain inpatient at investigator discretion.

data.name: TE ADA Follow_up Decision
data.description: At follow_up/ED, patients with treatment_emergent antidrug antibodies enter additional 12_weekly (84±7 days) immunogenicity follow_up until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Patient Replacement Decision
data.description: Patients discontinuing before completing both periods with evaluable primary outcome may be replaced, not exceeding 75 total enrolled.

data.name: Primary Non_inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Primary analysis of treatment success percentages in 66 completers; non_inferiority declared if upper limit of 2_sided 95% CI for difference (IMG _ LY900018) < 10%.
